root_cause.text: The `spi-s3c64xx` driver’s `remove()` path still unconditionally released DMA channels (`dma_release_channel()` on `sdd->rx_dma.ch`/`tx_dma.ch`) even after DMA allocation had been moved from `probe()` to `s3c64xx_spi_prepare_transfer()`, so on unbind those channel pointers could be NULL and trigger a NULL-dereference.
root_cause.evidence: The patch removes the `if (!is_polling(sdd)) { dma_release_channel(sdd->rx_dma.ch); dma_release_channel(sdd->tx_dma.ch); }` block from `drivers/spi/spi-s3c64xx.c::s3c64xx_spi_remove()`, and the commit message explicitly says the earlier change “failed to remove the corresponding deallocation from remove()” and that the bogus release caused a “NULL-pointer dereference on driver unbind.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove redundant DMA channel release from s3c64xx SPI device removal to fix teardown handling.
intent_record.what: The remove() function for the s3c64xx SPI platform driver no longer conditionally calls dma_release_channel() for the RX and TX DMA channels when the driver is not in polling mode. The pm_runtime teardown calls remain unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, device removal will skip explicit DMA channel release in this path, leaving DMA channel cleanup to some other mechanism or earlier lifecycle step. This changes the teardown behavior for non-polling SPI devices by removing the direct DMA resource deallocation from remove().

grouping_result.intent: Remove redundant DMA channel release from s3c64xx SPI device removal to fix teardown handling.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly matches the root cause: it removes the unconditional DMA channel release in the SPI remove() path, which could otherwise dereference NULL channel pointers after DMA allocation was moved out of probe().

candidates.rationale: This unconditionally releases the RX DMA channel during remove(); after DMA allocation moved out of probe(), this pointer can be NULL on unbind, causing a NULL-dereference.
This unconditionally releases the TX DMA channel during remove(); once DMA channels are only allocated for transfers, the pointer may be NULL at teardown and dereferencing it can crash.

vuln_statements.explanation: This remove() path unconditionally releases the RX DMA channel even though DMA allocation may no longer have occurred during probe(); if sdd->rx_dma.ch is NULL on unbind, dma_release_channel() can dereference it and crash.

This remove() path unconditionally releases the TX DMA channel even though DMA allocation may now happen only for transfers; if sdd->tx_dma.ch is NULL on teardown, dma_release_channel() can dereference it and crash.
